difficulty_reason: registration is toggling OAuth on in Connect settings and copying a Stripe-issued client_id - no app review for connecting Standard accounts; the technical work is the token exchange, not the setup
setup_time: unknown - Stripe documents no registration timeline; enabling OAuth and getting a test client_id is self-serve in the dashboard, while live mode requires completing account activation (business verification), whose duration is undocumented

approval.kind: Stripe App Marketplace review, required only to publish a Stripe App publicly on the marketplace; connecting users via Connect OAuth needs no review at all
approval.wait: 4 business days for the marketplace app review (documented); resubmission and re-review are required after changes to the app or listing
approval.notes: Stripe has two distinct 'OAuth app' worlds. (1) Connect OAuth for Standard accounts: enable OAuth in Connect settings, get a client_id, connect users immediately - no review. Note that Stripe does NOT recommend OAuth for new Connect platforms (Connect Onboarding is the recommended path), and since June 2021 platforms using read_write scope cannot connect Standard accounts controlled by another platform. (2) Stripe Apps on the App Marketplace: uses the marketplace OAuth v2 flow (Stripe deprecated the Connect authentication method for apps), and public listing requires passing a human app review with a documented 4-business-day turnaround. Private apps installed only by your own team skip the marketplace and its review entirely.
approval.wait_short: none for Connect OAuth; 4 business days for marketplace listing

summary: Stripe is a tale of two OAuth paths, and picking the right one matters more than the setup itself. Connect OAuth (client_id from Connect settings) works immediately with no review but is explicitly not recommended for new platforms. A public Stripe App on the marketplace means a real human review with a documented 4-business-day decision, quality requirements, and test credentials handed to reviewers. Either way, live mode first requires activating your account with verified business details.

steps.title: Choose your path before touching settings
steps.detail: If you are building a Connect platform, Stripe recommends Connect Onboarding over OAuth for Standard accounts - OAuth is legacy for that use case. If you are building an integration for many Stripe users, a Stripe App (marketplace OAuth v2) is the modern route; private apps for your own team skip the marketplace entirely.

steps.title: Activate your Stripe account for live mode
steps.detail: Sandboxes work immediately for testing. To use any service in live mode you must verify your business and complete activation requirements; marketplace publishing additionally requires a verified email and business details.

steps.title: Enable OAuth in Connect settings and copy your client_id
steps.detail: In the dashboard's Connect OAuth onboarding options, enable onboarding accounts with OAuth, copy the Stripe-generated client_id (separate live and test IDs exist; use the sandbox client_id against sandbox accounts), and register every redirect URI - Stripe falls back to the first configured URI when the parameter is omitted.

steps.title: Complete your platform profile
steps.detail: Stripe requires completing your platform's profile (in Connect settings) before onboarding connected accounts - it is what users see when deciding whether to connect to your platform.

steps.title: Build the connection flow
steps.detail: Send users to connect.stripe.com/oauth/authorize with response_type=code, your client_id, scope=read_write (platforms MUST use read_write; read_only is reserved for registered extensions and omission errors out), and a unique state value for CSRF protection. Users with no Stripe account create one inside the authorization flow.

steps.title: Exchange the code and store the credentials
steps.detail: POST the short-lived, single-use authorization code to connect.stripe.com/oauth/token with your secret key. Store the returned stripe_user_id (the connected account ID, used in the Stripe-Account header) and the refresh_token - Stripe only hands you the refresh token in this initial response, and it is needed to roll access tokens later.

steps.title: Handle disconnection both ways
steps.detail: Watch the account.application.deauthorized webhook to clean up when a user disconnects you, and offer disconnect yourself by POSTing client_id and stripe_user_id to connect.stripe.com/oauth/deauthorize.

steps.title: For a marketplace listing, pass the app review
steps.detail: Submit the listing form (using the live-mode public install URL on the marketplace OAuth v2 flow, not Connect onboarding), provide test credentials with MFA disabled and recordings of complex flows, and meet the qualitative review requirements: transparent pricing, no ads, clear navigation with no dead ends, proper loading and error states, sandbox support declared in the manifest. Expect an approval or feedback email in 4 business days; any change to the app or listing means resubmitting and passing review again.

requirements: A Stripe account; live mode requires completing activation (verified business details)
OAuth enabled in Connect settings with at least one registered redirect URI (all URIs must be pre-registered)
A completed platform profile before onboarding connected accounts
Server-side storage for stripe_user_id and refresh_token per connected account
A webhook endpoint for account.application.deauthorized events
For marketplace publishing: test credentials with MFA disabled, testing guidance covering all key features, and compliance with the app quality requirements
nuances: Stripe explicitly does not recommend OAuth for new Connect platforms - Connect Onboarding for Standard accounts is the recommended path, so OAuth registration is mostly a legacy/extension concern.
Since June 2021, platforms using read_write scope cannot connect Standard accounts that are controlled by another platform; extensions are unaffected.
The scope rules are inverted from intuition: platforms must request read_write, and read_only exists only for registered extensions - omitting scope shows the user an error, not a consent screen.
The refresh_token is delivered exactly once, in the initial token exchange response - lose it and you cannot roll access tokens without the user reconnecting.

For marketplace apps, Stripe deprecated the Connect authentication method entirely: apps must use the marketplace OAuth v2 authorize URL, and reviewers install through your live-mode public install link.
The 4-business-day review decision is one of the few documented review timelines in this library - but every change to the app or listing restarts it.

common_blockers.problem: The authorization page shows an error instead of a consent screen.
common_blockers.solution: The scope parameter is missing or read_only: platforms must pass scope=read_write explicitly. Also confirm the redirect_uri matches one pre-registered in Connect settings.

common_blockers.problem: Connecting a user's account fails for some users only.
common_blockers.solution: Since June 2021, read_write platforms cannot connect Standard accounts controlled by another platform - those users must connect through that platform's flow, not yours.

common_blockers.problem: Access tokens cannot be rolled after the initial connection.
common_blockers.solution: The refresh_token only appears in the initial token-exchange response. If it was not persisted, the user must reconnect; store it alongside stripe_user_id from day one.

common_blockers.problem: Marketplace review keeps coming back with feedback.
common_blockers.solution: The most common review issues are listing quality and reviewer access: provide test credentials (MFA disabled) that connect through the app installation itself, attach screen recordings of complex flows, and check the qualitative requirements - transparent pricing, no dead-end navigation, real error and loading states.

agent_can_do: Implement the full connection flow: authorize redirect with state, code exchange, Stripe-Account header usage, and deauthorize handling
Prefill the Stripe account form via stripe_user[...] parameters to cut onboarding drop-off
Set up the deauthorized webhook handler and cleanup logic
Draft the marketplace listing content and record the testing-guidance walkthroughs to the review checklist
human_must_do: Own the Stripe account, complete business verification, and accept the platform's liability for connected-account fraud
Complete the platform profile and decide live vs sandbox rollout
Hold the secret API key used in token exchanges
Submit the marketplace listing and respond to review feedback within the 4-business-day cycle

evidence.claim: Connect OAuth setup is self-serve in the dashboard: enable OAuth in the Connect OAuth onboarding options, copy the Stripe-generated client_id (separate live and test IDs), and pre-register all redirect URIs.

Stripe does not recommend OAuth for new Connect platforms (Connect Onboarding is recommended instead), and since June 2021 platforms using read_write scope cannot connect platform-controlled Standard accounts.
Platforms must pass scope=read_write; read_only is available only to registered extensions, and omitting scope or requesting read_only shows an error instead of the authorization page.

The token exchange returns stripe_user_id and a refresh_token that is only available in that initial response; disconnection works via the account.application.deauthorized webhook and the oauth/deauthorize endpoint.
Completing the platform's profile is a prerequisite for onboarding connected accounts.
Live mode requires verifying the business and completing activation requirements; marketplace publishing requires a verified email and business details.

Public marketplace listing requires a human app review with a documented 4-business-day email decision; changes to the app or listing require resubmission and passing review again; reviewers need test credentials with MFA disabled and must connect through the app installation (marketplace OAuth v2), not Connect onboarding.
The app review enforces qualitative requirements: transparent pricing, no ads, clear navigation without dead ends, real loading/error states, declared sandbox support in the manifest.
The Connect settings area of the Stripe dashboard resolves unauthenticated (the settings themselves sit behind login, like other providers' consoles).

uncertainties: How long account activation (business verification) takes is undocumented - it varies by country and business type, so the live-mode wait is unknown even though the marketplace review wait is not.

Whether Stripe performs any screening before a Connect OAuth client_id can connect live accounts (beyond activation and the platform profile) is not documented; no review is described, but an undocumented gate cannot be ruled out.
The June 2021 read_write restriction's exact definition of 'controlled by another platform' is not spelled out on the page - edge cases (migrated accounts, multiple platforms) are unclear.
The 4-business-day review timeline is stated for the initial decision email; total time-to-listing with feedback cycles is not bounded by the docs.
